variants.tailReminder: Keep outputs short and dense. Lead with the outcome. No filler, no emoji, no process narration.

variants.note: Restate the contract in CLAUDE.md, which Claude Code wraps in an explicit override directive and re-injects as a user message.
variants.claudeMd:
# Response style

The active output style is binding. Every reply must obey it:

- Lead with the outcome in the first sentence.
- Sentences under 20 words. No filler, no emoji, no celebration.
- Do not narrate process. Report findings and results only.
- Status updates answer: what I did / did it work / what you do next.

//run: maxCellSeconds is the cell's runaway guard: a wall-clock ceiling on one
cell, enforced by an AbortController in run.mjs. It is the only hard stop
the SDK offers — maxTurns bounds tool rounds but not the time spent inside
one, and taskBudget only tells the model its remaining tokens and asks it
to pace itself, which a wedged loop will not do. A cell that trips it
comes back with error 'error_timeout' and is excluded from every mean,
the same as any other errored cell.
It bounds a cell, not a run. The judge call in judge.mjs and the rewrite
call in improve.mjs take no abortController and no timeout, so a model
call that stalls on either path still hangs the run. That gap predates
this guard — maxBudgetUsd never covered them either — and closing it is
COS-26.
600 is a backstop, not a tuned figure. Every row now records elapsedMs,
so lower it against those durations once a run has produced some.
judgeModel is sonnet, and COS-20 measured what that costs. Of the four
tiers it re-judged the same 60 saved replies with, Sonnet is the LEAST
repeatable: judge-call SD 10.17 points against Opus 5.49, Haiku 7.29 and
Fable 4.18. It is left as sonnet on purpose — every published judge figure
in this project was scored by it, and changing it makes none of them
comparable with the next run. Change it only alongside re-establishing
them, and re-read the ledger's judge-validation row first: a change of
judge moves three published conclusions.
//improve: models is this loop's own list and is not the matrix's. Every arm runs
across the whole of it, and an arm is one split measured once: two for the
baseline, two per iteration (train and holdout), two more at the reserve
gate. At maxIterations 6 that is 16 arms, 14 of them before the gate, so
adding a tier here is a much larger commitment than adding one to the
top-level models. Omitting the key warns and falls back to the smallest
tier alone; --models overrides it, and --models with nothing in it is an
error rather than a silent fall-back to this list.
trainSplit and holdoutSplit are the loop's own signals. reserveSplit is not:
the loop never selects it, and it is measured once at the end to validate the
candidate the loop wants to adopt. minReserveDelta is deliberately as tight as
minHoldoutDelta even though it sits inside the noise floor — rejecting a sound
rewrite means a re-run, adopting a bad one ships a regression.
